problem.text: A palindrome between $1000$ and $10{,}000$ is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is divisible by $7$?

steps.title: Where to start: write the palindrome with digit variables
steps.body: Every number between $1000$ and $10{,}000$ that is a palindrome has four digits, so it looks like $abba$. The clue is that the digits come in matching pairs. Writing the number in expanded form lets us group the matching digits together.

your_turn.prompt: Expand $abba$ in powers of $10$ and collect the $a$ terms and the $b$ terms.

steps.title: Look at each part modulo 7
steps.body: Now check how $1001$ and $110$ behave when divided by $7$. A term that is always a multiple of $7$ can be ignored.

steps.title: Which digits b work?
steps.body: Since $1001a$ is always a multiple of $7$, the palindrome is divisible by $7$ exactly when $110b$ is, which means $5b$ must be a multiple of $7$. Because $5$ and $7$ share no factor, $b$ itself must be a multiple of $7$. Notice that $a$ does not matter at all.

your_turn.prompt: Which digits $b$ from $0$ to $9$ are multiples of $7$?
your_turn.answer: $b = 0$ and $b = 7$. Careful: $0$ counts as a multiple of $7$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The digit $a$ can be anything from $1$ to $9$ either way, so the probability depends only on $b$. Out of the $10$ equally likely choices for $b$, exactly $2$ work, so the probability is $\frac{2}{10} = \frac{1}{5}$. The answer is **(E)** $\frac{1}{5}$.

wrong_choices.A: This comes from finding only $b = 7$ and forgetting $b = 0$. The number $0$ is a multiple of $7$, and $1001a$ itself (for example $1001$) is divisible by $7$.
